# Issue #7: touching intervals are not merged

`merge_intervals([(1, 3), (3, 5)])` returns `[(1, 3), (3, 5)]` but the documented
behaviour is that closed intervals sharing an endpoint merge into `[(1, 5)]`.
Unsorted input must also be handled. Fix `ranges/merge.py`.

ranges/merge.py
tests/test_merge.py

   2|     """Merge a list of closed integer intervals (start, end).
   3|     Touching intervals, e.g. (1,3) and (3,5), merge into (1,5).
   4|     Input may be unsorted. Returns a sorted list of tuples."""
   5|     if not intervals:
   6|         return []
   7|     merged = [tuple(intervals[0])]
   8|     for start, end in intervals[1:]:

  10|         if start < last_end:
  11|             merged[-1] = (last_start, max(last_end, end))
  12|         else:
  13|             merged.append((start, end))

content: All tests pass and the sanity checks confirm correct behavior: touching intervals merge, unsorted input is handled, nested intervals collapse, and empty/single inputs work.

arguments.summary: Fixed `ranges/merge.py` in two ways: (1) changed the merge condition from `start < last_end` to `start <= last_end` so closed intervals sharing an endpoint (e.g. (1,3) and (3,5)) merge into (1,5), and (2) sorted the full input list before merging so unsorted input is handled correctly (the previous code only processed `intervals[1:]` and seeded with the unsorted first element). Verified with the existing test suite (2 tests pass) and manual checks for unsorted, nested, empty, and single-interval inputs.
